summary: Vendor portal XML attachment charset truncation causing missing invoice line items during quarterly settlement
description:
Issue summary: Several supplier EDI/XML invoices uploaded through the vendor portal in the past 48h have missing or truncated invoice line items after ingestion. Impact: Three vendors scheduled for the quarterly settlement cycle show reduced totals (line items silently stripped) leading to underpayment risk and manual reconciliation load for AP. Estimated value affected: ~€210k across 7 invoices.

Observed behavior: When vendor portal processes XML attachments with windows-1252 charset declaration but payload actually contains mixed UTF-8 multibyte characters (e.g., vendor address fields with em-dash and non-latin accents), the upstream attachment handler truncates the XML at the first invalid byte boundary. The downstream OCR/parser sees a truncated <InvoiceLines> section and imports only the first N lines.

Business urgency: High — this intersects quarter close. Manual workarounds are possible for isolated invoices, but scale makes this a P1.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Upload attached sample XML (attached_sample_win1252_mixedchars.xml) to vendor portal using vendor account 'vendor-gh-384'.
2) Portal logs show content-type: application/xml; charset=windows-1252 and content-length 64,132.
3) Ingestion service (api-ingest) receives a truncated body with content-length reduced by bytes after first multibyte marker.
4) AP pipeline maps <InvoiceLines> element containing only 1 of 8 line items.
5) Reconcile output total vs original expected total to observe mismatch.
logs:
[2026-03-11T09:12:34Z] api-gateway: POST /portal/upload 200 id=tx_9a3c
[2026-03-11T09:12:35Z] ingest-service: read 64132 bytes expected, actual 36792 bytes, warning: 'invalid byte sequence' in convert_encoding
[2026-03-11T09:12:35Z] ocr-parser: parsed InvoiceLines count=1 expected=8 invoice_id=INV-2026-0007
[2026-03-11T09:12:36Z] ap-worker: flagged mismatch, created task INT-160005 for follow-up
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by AP flagged pattern related to charset headers. Replayed a copy of the uploaded payload from vendor portal S3 bucket (s3://redwood-prod/vendor-uploads/2026/03/11/tx_9a3c.xml). When forcing a UTF-8 decode, ingestion succeeds. Forcing windows-1252 decode on the same bytes triggers conversion error and stream read stops at first invalid sequence. Hypothesis: vendor portal or nginx edge is normalizing/declaring charset=windows-1252 for certain vendor tenants, while client tool actually sends UTF-8 bytes. The ingestion pipeline uses iconv-based conversion with 'stop on error' semantics; should be tolerant and replace invalid sequences instead.

Commands run:
- hexdump snippet shows 0xE2 0x80 0x94 sequence (UTF-8 em-dash) present in payload despite windows-1252 header.
- curl --data-binary @sample.xml to /upload reproduced problem when header set to windows-1252.

Temporary mitigation tested: re-encoding the stored object to UTF-8 (iconv -f windows-1252 -t UTF-8//IGNORE) restores all lines; reprocessing the job produces correct totals.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Khan (AP): Raised after noticing 3 supplier totals not matching their portal copies during quarter close sampling. Attached one sample and initial discrepancy notes.
2026-03-10 - Liam Chen (Infra): Confirmed receipt of artifacts. Replayed upload from S3 and reproduced truncation locally. Suspect charset mismatch in upload header vs payload bytes.

2026-03-11 - Priya Rao (Vendor Success): Reached out to vendor GH for confirmation. Vendor says their system exports in UTF-8; shows example with em-dash characters. Asked vendor to stop using windows-1252 headers if possible.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen (Infra): Scoped change: ingest service uses a strict convert that fails on invalid sequences. Engineering to prepare safe fallback to 'replace' mode and add validation at portal ingress. Filing infra PR and scheduling hotfix. Linked INT-246801 for ingest retry framework.
2026-03-12 - Marta Silva (AP Manager): Requesting manual reprocessing of the 7 impacted invoices before EOD close. Created a manual runbook note under Confluence.
resolution:
Workaround: AP performed manual re-encoding and reprocessed the 7 affected invoices (scripts stored in /ops/ap/reprocess_2026Q1.sh). Hotfix planned: ingest-service change to use tolerant decoding (replace invalid sequences) and portal will validate charset header vs content on upload. Infra PR opened: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821.

Next steps: 1) Deploy hotfix to staging and run full ingest regression suite (task INT-160012). 2) Add ingestion metric to alert on 'bytes_read != content-length' for automated detection. 3) Vendor Success to notify top 50 vendors about preferred UTF-8 encoding.
